rationale: Python is the reference implementation the other languages are measured against, so its named-function floor is exact 1.0 rather than a margin below measurement: every `def` is an entity, including nested ones (ATL-096, commit a23d528). Lambdas are anonymous and get no entity by design; their calls attribute to the enclosing function, which is why `calls` is high despite 8 uncaptured lambda nodes. The 3.4% call shortfall is entirely module-scope: 0 call nodes sit inside a function that produced no entity, and 11 of the 14 module-scope calls are unemitted. Eleven uids collide and all eleven are correct merges, not debt: `command` and `group` each carry four `@t.overload` declarations ahead of the real implementation, `get_current_context` two, and `_get_argv_encoding` is defined once per branch of an `if WIN:` platform conditional. An overload is a signature for the same function, not a second function, so one node is the right answer.
